title: In this French city, social diversity in schools has almost disappeared
subhead: According to studies, the southern city of Perpignan is the most educationally segregated in France. It's divided between private schools, which rank among the most privileged in the country, and public schools, which, in almost every case, sit at the exact opposite end of the social scale.

Mistral AI raises €3 billion in response to doubts over its strategic direction
subhead: The French artificial intelligence start-up, accused by some experts of having abandoned the race against its American and Chinese rivals to focus on data centers and services, insists it has not given up on producing cutting-edge models. It has secured its largest-ever funding round and welcomed Samsung as a shareholder.

title: In Germany, AfD's performance in Saxony-Anhalt weakens Friedrich Merz
subhead: 'Deeply shocked' by the far right's regional victory on Sunday, the chancellor now has to contend with his coalition partner, the Social Democratic Party, which wants to renegotiate pension reform. For its part, Alternative for Germany says it aims to reach 40% of the vote at the federal level by 2029.

title: The return of whale hunting in Iceland stirs public debate
subhead: Lacking market opportunities, the last whaling company still in operation decided not to use its fishing quotas for 2024 and 2025. But during summer 2026, the company Hvalur hf. killed more than 50 whales, reigniting discussions over a total ban.

Annie Ernaux's words resonate among new generation of women: 'She doesn't try to make it poetic'
subhead: Annie Ernaux's books, which delve into the intimate side of the female experience, have found unprecedented resonance among women. The work of the Nobel laureate in literature echoed through the voices of two actresses – Tess Barthélemy in a film directed by her mother, Judith Godrèche, and Suzanne de Baecque in a solo stage performance – as well as in the powerful readings by high school girls in a documentary by Claire Simon.

title: Far right achieves historic result in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt regional elections
subhead: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, founded in 2013, recorded its best-ever result in this former East German state on Sunday, September 6, as Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party collapsed. However, the AfD cannot govern alone at this stage.
